Developer setup

Source: SETUP.md

This file documents the one-time steps needed to turn the hand-authored scaffold into a compilable Stan package, plus the toolchain notes for this machine. It is excluded from the built package via .Rbuildignore.

1. Toolchain (Windows)

Stan models are compiled to C++ at install time, so a matching Rtools is required.

  • This machine has R 4.4.3 and R 4.1.3 installed, but only Rtools40.
  • R 4.4 officially pairs with Rtools44 — using Rtools40 with R 4.4 is a common cause of Stan compile failures.

Choose one:

  • Recommended: install Rtools44 from https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/rtools44/rtools44.html and use R 4.4.3, or
  • build under R 4.1.3 (which matches the installed Rtools40).

Verify with:

pkgbuild::has_build_tools(debug = TRUE)

Windows “file too big” — required big-object flag

On Windows the Stan-generated object file exceeds the COFF object-format limit and the assembler aborts with Fatal error: ... file too big. Fix it with the big-object assembler flag, supplied through a user-level Makevars (the package’s own src/Makevars.win is regenerated by rstan_config() at install, so a flag added there does not survive). tools/Makevars.win in this repo contains:

CXX17FLAGS += -Wa,-mbig-obj
CXX14FLAGS += -Wa,-mbig-obj
CXXFLAGS   += -Wa,-mbig-obj

Apply it for a build by pointing R_MAKEVARS_USER at that file, then install with a direct R CMD INSTALL (which honours R_MAKEVARS_USER, unlike pkgbuild::compile_dll, which overrides it):

R_MAKEVARS_USER=tools/Makevars.win \
  R CMD INSTALL --no-multiarch .

Or copy tools/Makevars.win to ~/.R/Makevars.win once, machine-wide.

2. Install dependencies

install.packages(c(
  "rstan", "rstantools", "StanHeaders", "posterior",
  "RcppParallel", "BH", "RcppEigen",
  "bayesplot", "lqmm", "nlme", "SBC", "testthat", "knitr", "rmarkdown"
))

lme4, Rcpp, devtools, roxygen2 are already installed.

3. Wire up the compiled model

The scaffold ships the Stan sources in inst/stan/ and all pure-R logic, but not the generated glue that rstantools produces (R/stanmodels.R, src/Makevars*, src/stanExports_*, configure/configure.win). Generate it in place:

# from the directory *containing* the bqmm/ folder
rstantools::rstan_create_package(
  path     = "bqmm",
  stan_files = character(0),   # we already placed files in inst/stan
  roxygen  = FALSE,
  travis   = FALSE
)

If rstan_create_package() refuses to populate a non-empty directory, run it against a temporary path and copy the generated configure, configure.win, src/Makevars, src/Makevars.win, R/stanmodels.R, and inst/include/stan_meta_header.hpp into this package, then add

#' @useDynLib bqmm, .registration = TRUE
#' @importFrom Rcpp sourceCpp

to R/bqmm-package.R (the commented lines in NAMESPACE already note this).

4. Build documentation and compile

devtools::document()   # regenerates NAMESPACE + man/ from roxygen
devtools::load_all()   # compiles inst/stan/bqmm.stan -> stanmodels$bqmm
devtools::test()

5. Sanity run

fit <- bqmm(distance ~ age + (1 | Subject),
            data = nlme::Orthodont, tau = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9),
            chains = 2, iter = 1000, seed = 1)
summary(fit)

Expect Rhat < 1.01, no divergent transitions, and adjusted vs. unadjusted vcov() intervals that differ in width.

What is real vs. stubbed in the scaffold

Area State
inst/stan/bqmm.stan, ald.stanfunctions Complete, ready to compile
R/formula.R, R/standata.R Real (use installed lme4) — unit-testable now
R/adjust.R (Yang-Wang-He) Real numeric logic; verify sigma scalar vs. paper
R/noncrossing.R (rearrangement) Real
R/family.R, R/priors.R Real
R/bqmm.R, R/fit.R Real orchestration; depend on compiled stanmodels$bqmm
R/methods-*.R Mix of real and .NotYetImplemented() stubs
tests/testthat/ Tests for formula / adjust / noncrossing run without Stan
